scale.basis: 385cm and97mm humerus are documented. Skull/jaw/paddle dimensions are approximate proportions interpreted from central skeleton photo, which has perspective distortion and no internal metricbar. Flesh width and thickness are conservative inference. These secondary values are not specimen caliper measurements.

morphology: Core identification: extremely long slender upper rostrum extends conspicuously beyond the shorter lower jaw. Lower jaw reaches roughly half the upper skull length from rear-skull landmark. Preserve this overhang in closed-mouth profile; do not merely gape equal-length jaws or elongate both into a generic dolphin beak.

Upper projection is a tooth-bearing jaw, not a separate horn/swordfish spike glued above the mouth. Thin tapered continuous rostrum, not broad crocodile snout. Lower jaw connects organically into rear head.

Large lateral orbital region with short cheek behind it, narrow short head-to-trunk transition. External eye is a modest globe within a larger orbitalregion, not the entire skeletal eye-ring copied onto skin.

Slender fusiform living trunk, elongated tailstock and downward skeletal tailbend into lower caudal lobe. Interpret actual skeletal architecture, not the photographed postmortem S-shaped tail pose or rectangular slab outlines.
Exactly four long narrow rounded paddles, anterior pair larger than posterior. Keep fleshy membranes enclosing digits; no exposed fingers, extra shark fins or copied bone texture.

A modest dorsal fin and upper tail membrane are conservative ichthyosaur soft-body inferences, not preserved outlines inR5465. No exactfin height/angle claimed. Avoid tall shark sail or enormous symmetric whale fluke; vertical caudal plane, lowerlobe supported by downward vertebral bend.
Small lateral nostrils anterior to eyes, not cetacean blowhole. Smooth scaleless-looking skin, no gill slits, scales, spikes, shell or external ribs.
Closed or nearly closed mouth makes short mandible unambiguous. Any teeth are very small/subdued and locally attached to jaw margins, not exaggerated saw teeth. No separate protruding tusks.
Neutral horizontal swimming pose. Four paddles mildly spread for visualcounting; no stand, fossil slab, museum case, titlecard or prey.
uncertainty: R5465 is a compressed mounted skeleton, not an intact living contour. Living tissue thickness, dorsalfin and upper caudalfin margins, exactskin pattern, external eye shape and swimming pose are reconstructions.
Taxonomic debate retained at specieslevel without changing genus. Do not mix E.mistelgauensis body estimates intoR5465.
No four-angle realphoto set exists here. Standard four renders inspect a bounded3D interpretation supported by real specimen plus primary literature, notphotogrammetry.

Mounted skeletal curvature or preparatory replacements cannot be treated as exact livingtail outline. Buchholtz2001 flags altered fluke orientation in anotherGPIT specimen and dubious authenticity of SMNS14931; neither becomes exactgeometry anchor.
